  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Washington Nationals @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

Cade Cavalli's return alone gives this game a story worth watching: a former top prospect back from Tommy John and finally healthy is squaring off against Tyler Glasnow, whose own career has been a rolling injury saga. Both teams post strong tNERD marks — Washington's 8.45 fueled by excellent baserunning and a young, cheap roster, LA's 8.19 driven by big-time batting production — and the pitching side is even better, with Glasnow's 9.18 pNERD the headline thanks to a sparkling xFIP- of 66. Cavalli isn't far behind at 7.82, riding a mid-90s heater and a stretch where he's allowed only five earned runs in his last six starts. This is Glasnow's first home start since returning from the injured list, adding some intrigue to how his surgically-rebuilt arm holds up. The Dodgers, despite losing six of their last nine games, still hold a comfortable lead atop the NL West, while the Nationals have lost five straight on the road and are fading from wild-card contention — so don't expect playoff desperation, just quality arms. At 16.82, the gNERD score sits well above both the historical average (10.81) and today's slate (10.87), making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Texas Rangers, 4:05p

Summary

Rasmussen and deGrom bring the ace stuff, and this one has October implications baked in — that's a rare combo worth clearing your evening for.

Tampa Bay rolls in at 84-57, holding a four-game AL East cushion, while Texas sits below .500 but still fighting for playoff position, so this series carries real weight beyond the pitching matchup. The Rangers hope the "vintage" Jacob deGrom returns for his next start, five days after the 38-year-old pitched one of the best games of his career. That gem saw him face the minimum through seven innings against Oakland, the first Rangers pitcher to do that since 2023. The stats back up the eye test — deGrom's pNERD of 10.82 is elite, built on nasty swinging-strike rates and mid-90s-plus heat, and it's boosted by some bad luck (a 4.00 ERA that his xFIP suggests he doesn't deserve). Rasmussen isn't far behind at 8.29, and Tampa's righty enters 14-5 with a 2.95 ERA, having gone 5-0 in six August starts. Team-wise, both sides are just okay, but with two frontline arms dueling, this gNERD of 14.66 ranks near the top of today's slate — prioritize the first few innings.

Chicago Cubs @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

Here's the summary:

A wild-card race game with a Triple-A callup on the mound and a hot-hitting third baseman worth tuning in for, even if the pitching matchup itself is middling. Javier Assad gets recalled from Iowa to start after Chicago's Javier Assad is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Iowa to start on Saturday, having spent the season shuttling between the Cubs and Iowa and moving from the rotation to the bullpen. His stuff hasn't been sharp in the surface metrics (a putrid swinging-strike rate drags his pNERD to 2.74), but he's been quietly effective drilling into contact management. Opposite him, Ryan Gusto owns the better peripherals of the two, with a strong strike-throwing rate driving his 4.86 pNERD, and he's allowed two earned runs or fewer in five straight starts. The real juice here is on the team side: Chicago's tNERD of 10.42 is elite, powered by standout fielding and batting runs, while the Cubs will try to keep their hold on the top wild-card spot when they visit the Marlins, having supplanted Philadelphia for the top wild-card position with a 6-1 win over the Marlins on Friday. Alex Bregman is locked in, hitting .400 (14-for-35) with five homers and 12 RBIs during an eight-game hitting streak, giving this playoff-race game (13.49 gNERD, comfortably above the day's average) more juice than the arms alone would suggest.

Los Angeles Angels @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Braxton Ashcraft is quietly having a breakout season for a Pirates team playing its best baseball, and that alone makes this game worth a look even with the Angels doing their best impression of a AAA squad. Ashcraft carries a 14-5 record and has been dominant lately, going 5-1 with a 2.66 ERA over his last seven starts, including a win at St. Louis where he allowed two runs on six hits in five innings. His 11.45 pNERD is comfortably above the 95th percentile for today's slate, powered by elite strike-throwing and a mid-90s heater backed by a sparkling xFIP-. On the other side, Kikuchi is 0-5 and still working back from a lost season; this will be his third start since he missed almost four months due to left shoulder inflammation, so his 5.56 pNERD (bolstered heavily by positive regression luck) comes with real uncertainty attached. The Pirates (6.69 tNERD) bring solid baserunning and bullpen value, while the Angels (1.06 tNERD) are cratering across the board — bad fielding, bad baserunning, bad batting — and have lost 10 of their last 11 and need to go at least 10-11 in their final 21 games to avoid the first 100-game loss season in franchise history. The 12.38 gNERD sits above average largely because of Ashcraft; watch for the pitching, not the plot.

Atlanta Braves @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:05p

Summary

Braves lead the NL East race, this is a playoff-weight series with Atlanta having won the opener, and Zack Wheeler brings ace-level underlying stuff even if his last few starts have been shakier than his season line suggests.

Wheeler's pNERD of 8.42 is comfortably above today's average of 5.28, driven by a sparkling 74 xFIP- and above-average velocity and whiff rate — the classic Wheeler package even if his ERA has crept up lately (he's been the "more accomplished pitcher in a deep slump," per one preview, with rough outings over his last five starts despite a season-long 3.31 ERA and 154 strikeouts). Pérez, by contrast, sits at a modest 3.54 pNERD; he's been effective in results — allowing one earned run or fewer in five of his last six starts — but the components here (weak swinging-strike and strike rates) suggest he's getting by on soft-contact management rather than dominant stuff. Team-wise, Atlanta (5.62 tNERD) and Philadelphia (5.20) are both roughly average, with the Phillies' punchless offense (a batting runs figure well below average) somewhat offset by strong baserunning and bullpen work, and a slightly negative team luck for both clubs hinting at better days ahead offensively. The gNERD of 11.40 lands a touch above the historical median (10.80) and just below today's slate average (10.87) — solidly middle-of-the-pack, but the playoff stakes and division rivalry nudge this one up the must-watch list regardless of what the spreadsheet says.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's the class of this matchup, but neither starter is doing much to make it a pitching showcase, so watch this one for the Brewers' machine rather than a duel. Milwaukee arrives with an 87-54 record atop the NL Central and has thoroughly owned this series, having won four straight games in Cincinnati this season and gone 7-1 against the Reds overall, backed by a tNERD near the top of today's slate thanks to strong baserunning, bullpen work, and a young, cost-effective roster. Cincinnati's tNERD sits closer to league-average, dragged down by shaky bullpen and batting numbers, though Eugenio Suarez's power (he's tied Ken Griffey Jr. with his 21st homer of the season) keeps things from being a total snooze at the plate. On the mound, Dustin May brings a useful pNERD boost from his velocity, but he's fallen to 0-2 in his past four starts after a rough outing against Texas, and his time in Milwaukee has been ugly so far. Andrew Abbott is the weaker link here, having lost his third straight start last time out, tying season highs in runs and hits allowed in a 17-5 shellacking by the Cubs. Overall gNERD lands almost exactly at the historic median — watchable mostly for the Brewers' quality, not the pitching matchup.

New York Yankees @ San Diego Padres, 4:15p

Summary

Both New York and San Diego are jockeying for playoff position with something real to play for, but this particular pitching matchup won't leave you glued to your seat—Rodón and Ray are two aging lefties trading league-average results rather than dominance. It's a solidly middle-of-the-pack gNERD score of 10.87, right at today's average, carried almost entirely by the offenses and bullpens rather than the arms on the mound.

San Diego arrives having gone 3-7 in their last 10 games, with a bullpen that just burned through extra innings the previous night, which undercuts the shiny Padres tNERD of 9.57 built on strong fielding and bullpen z-scores. Ray's 20 home runs allowed in 149 innings translates to a HR/9 rate around 1.21, and his pNERD of just 0.95 reflects a below-average strike-throwing rate and a plodding pace that will test your patience between pitches. Rodón's 3.28 pNERD isn't much better, hampered by a similarly poor strike percentage, though his sharper swinging-strike rate at least offers some swing-and-miss appeal. In a matchup where New York may need one big middle-of-the-order blow against Robbie Ray, Rice is the Yankees bat that jumps off the page, leading the team with 36 home runs. Watch for the offense and late innings, not the starters.

Detroit Tigers @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:10p

Summary

A rookie-of-the-year candidate with legitimately electric stuff facing a fading team that just got swept in a doubleheader — this one leans watchable mostly because of Parker Messick. Messick, Cleveland's 25-year-old lefty, has been the story of Cleveland's summer, and his pNERD of 8.23 backs it up — his xFIP- of 82 and a quick 16.8-second pace make him one of the day's more compelling arms to watch, with his final component of 8.23 sitting well above the "today's games" pitcher average of 5.28. He's coming off an impressive 2.02 ERA along with a tidy 2.68 FIP over six August starts, though the Tigers have had modest success against him this year with a bloated FIP against but respectable contact. On the other side, Framber Valdez brings a pedestrian pNERD of 3.30 and has actually struggled against this very Cleveland lineup, posting a 6.75 ERA and 6.25 FIP over 10 2/3 innings in two starts against them this season. Cleveland's tNERD of 7.01 outpaces Detroit's 2.96, largely thanks to a young, cheap roster and strong baserunning, while Detroit arrives limping after losing both ends of Friday's doubleheader, including a game where they blew a 6-1 lead. Overall gNERD of 10.75 is right around the historic median — watch for Messick, not much else.

Minnesota Twins @ Chicago White Sox, 4:10p

Summary

Good news for the White Sox has never made it more watchable than the Twins wish it were. Chicago leads the AL Central and just walloped Minnesota, while the Twins limp in banged-up and playoff-hopeful in name only.

The White Sox are the clear draw here, with a tNERD of 8.25 that's well above the historic 95th percentile mark of 9.7 territory, fueled by youth, barrel rate, and a bullpen that's actually been productive. Minnesota's 3.22 tNERD is the drag on this one, hurt by shaky fielding and baserunning, and further complicated by a lineup that is walking out without Byron Buxton, Austin Martin, Joe Ryan, and Cole Sands, though it still has real pieces in Kody Clemens, Ryan Jeffers, and Trevor Larnach. Chicago, meanwhile, comes in with real momentum behind them — the White Sox will try to keep their power surge going after a 4-1 win in Friday's series opener, in which they hit three home runs.

On the mound, Taj Bradley is the reason to tune in, sporting a strong 7.20 pNERD thanks largely to elite velocity (97.2 mph, well above the pack) and useful strikeout stuff — he's compiled a 10–6 record with a 3.85 ERA, a 1.26 WHIP, and 178 strikeouts, ninth-most in MLB. Anthony Kay is the far weaker complementary arm at 2.50 pNERD, and he's winless in his past four starts, with a slower pace and shakier command. Overall gNERD of 10.58 sits almost exactly at the historic median — decent, unspectacular, worth a look mainly for Bradley and Chicago's offense.

Jordan Walker delivered a two-run home run in the Cardinals' 13-8 win over Los Angeles earlier this week, so there's some offensive thump to watch for, even if the pitching matchup itself won't be the draw.

Toronto Blue Jays @ Kansas City Royals, 4:10p

Summary

I have enough here.

A wild-card scrap between a scuffling Toronto club and a Kansas City team playing out the string, with two veteran pitchers who've both seen better days. The Blue Jays are clawing for their playoat life while the Royals are just trying to spoil the party, and the pitching matchup does little to inspire confidence in either direction.

Toronto sits 13.5 games back in the division but is very much alive in the wild card conversation, having gone 21-13 since July 27, and they enter having gone 7-3 over their last ten games riding a three-game winning streak — including a Friday blowout where nine different Blue Jays recorded a hit. On the mound, Max Scherzer is the headline name but not the reason to tune in: Scherzer is 2-7 with a 6.16 ERA — a difficult stretch for a veteran who has been one of the game's most decorated starters, and his xFIP-backed pNERD of 1.37 reflects real skill decline, not just bad luck (well, actually some good luck, since his 23.0 luck score suggests he's earned an even worse line than his ERA shows). Seth Lugo is modestly more interesting statistically, his quick pace and respectable peripherals pushing him to a 4.14 pNERD, though he has struck out 118 batters but carries a 5.03 ERA of his own. Both teams' offenses and shaky bullpens (Kansas City's especially, a full two standard deviations below average) suggest a laugher is as likely as a pitcher's duel. At a 6.36 gNERD — well below both the historical and today's average — this one's a bottom-of-the-list watch unless you're a Jays fan sweating the standings.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Philadelphia Phillies, 3:40p

Summary

Two aces, a division race, and a genuine ace-vs-ace duel make this the best watch on the board today. Chris Sale and Cristopher Sánchez sit at Nos. 3 and 2, respectively, in MLB.com's most recent NL Cy Young poll, and this is round two of their season series—their first meeting ended with Sánchez allowing three runs, all unearned, over six innings, while Sale countered with seven innings of one-run ball. The stakes are real too: the Braves and Phillies are entering a critical stretch with seven meetings in 10 games, and Atlanta currently holds a four-game lead in the NL East. Sale has been quietly dominant, having allowed more than three earned runs just once all season, with the Angels tagging him for six in four innings back in April, while Sánchez has been nails at home, going 11-1 with a 1.68 ERA in home starts this season. The gNERD of 15.75 sits in the upper tier both historically (95th percentile is 15.6) and among today's slate (season-high 15.75), driven almost entirely by two elite arms with xFIP- in the 60s and swinging-strike rates well above average. Neither team's offense is thrilling on paper, but with this pitching and this postseason context, that hardly matters.

Logan Allen counters with almost no track record against this Tigers lineup and an unranked pNERD, so treat his outing as a mystery box. Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:15p

Summary

Milwaukee's charging into Wrigley with the majors' best rookie storyline on the mound, and this one lands near the top of today's slate for good reason. Logan Henderson has been a revelation, carrying a 9-2 record, 2.48 ERA, and 3.29 FIP across 14 starts, and he's been remarkably stingy with free passes — a 2.48 ERA and 0.83 WHIP across 76.1 innings while walking just 14 batters all season against 86 strikeouts. His pNERD of 8.77 reflects that combination of elite command and swing-and-miss stuff, well above today's average. Gausman, by contrast, has been the definition of inconsistent since arriving from Toronto — a 3-1 record with a 5.14 ERA and 4.08 FIP over five Cubs starts, alternating rough outings with a couple of gems — though his pNERD still checks in at a respectable 6.77, boosted by some bad luck that suggests better days ahead. On the team side, Chicago's tNERD (10.44) is carried by standout batting and fielding runs, while Milwaukee's (9.82) leans on baserunning and a strong bullpen, though the Cubs' pen is a real liability. Combined, this gNERD of 17.90 sits comfortably above both the historic 95th percentile and today's field — genuinely one of the day's best watches.

Summary

Tarik Skubal at Dodger Stadium against a Cardinals lineup missing key pieces is about as good a watchability bet as you'll find on the slate today. The Dodgers ace, now in his second month in LA after the trade-deadline blockbuster, has been every bit the marquee arm: Skubal has a 3.00 ERA and 37 strikeouts over 30 innings as a Dodger, and owns a 2.84 ERA with 153 strikeouts across 126.2 innings pitched overall this season. His last time out, he threw six innings against the Detroit Tigers, giving up one earned run while allowing four hits. Opposite him is Quinn Mathews, making his fifth start for the Cardinals, sitting at 1-2 with a 5.03 ERA and 20 strikeouts in 19 2/3 innings — a rookie with no track record yet, hence the flat 0.00 pNERD. The Dodgers' offense (tNERD 8.16) and bullpen give them the clear team-level edge over St. Louis's older, lighter-payroll but well-fielding Cardinals (6.35). With a gNERD of 15.87, well above both the historic and today's averages, this is a legitimate top-of-the-slate watch, carried almost entirely by Skubal.

Alcantara, meanwhile, has been the opposite story—the Marlins have struggled to win with their ace on the mound, losing four straight starts he's made—even though his stuff remains loud, with a 97-plus mph fastball driving his pNERD edge. Both starters pound the zone and rarely walk anyone, which oddsmakers think points to a lower-scoring affair, though the first two games of this series produced nine and 15 runs, and Kansas City is without its established closer, so that low-scoring read is far from guaranteed. On the NERD side, Miami's tNERD (9.14) towers over Kansas City's (4.08), largely because the Royals' bullpen has been a sinkhole while Miami's roster skews young, cheap, and unlucky enough to expect better days ahead. Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

This is about as good as it gets on paper, and the numbers back it up: a 20.60 gNERD score, comfortably atop today's slate and near the historic ceiling. Jacob Misiorowski, sporting a pNERD of 15.28 built on triple-digit velocity and elite swing-and-miss rates, is making his first start of September, with an opportunity to beat the Cubs for the third time this year, entering with a Majors lead in ERA, strikeouts, WHIP and opponents' average. He's now just a few weeks from what appears to be an NL Cy Young-winning season, 14-5 with a 1.73 ERA and 2.14 FIP over 151 innings, and even Pedro Martinez is publicly hyping him up. David Peterson, by contrast, offers a modest 5.51 pNERD and is mostly along for the ride, though since being acquired by the Cubs in late June he's pitched to a better 3.90 ERA and 4.31 FIP than his ugly season-long numbers suggest. Both tNERD marks sit well above average — Chicago's fueled by strong batting and fielding runs, Milwaukee's by baserunning and bullpen depth — and with the Brewers holding an eight-game NL Central lead, this is a marquee pitcher plus two solid lineups. Watch it.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Toronto Blue Jays @ Cleveland Guardians, 3:40p

Summary

Cleveland's Gavin Williams brings some of the best raw stuff in baseball to this one, and that alone should be enough to get this game bumped up your watchlist. The Guardians righty has racked up 204 strikeouts and a sparkling 3.98 ERA (and a much shinier 69 xFIP-) this year, pairing 97-mph heat with elite whiff and strike rates that produce the day's best pNERD score, 12.37 — well above today's average of 5.57 and squarely in the sport's upper tier. Opposite him is Spencer Miles, a 2026 rookie for Toronto still getting his feet wet in the majors, but his 78 xFIP- and mid-90s velocity make him a solid, sneaky-good foil rather than a laugher. Team-wise, neither Toronto nor Cleveland hits for much thump — both post barrel rates among the worst in the sample — but Cleveland's young, cheap, athletic roster (tNERD 7.14) offsets Toronto's star-power-but-underwhelming-output group (tNERD 3.60). Add it up and you get a gNERD of 15.63, comfortably above both the historical average (10.81) and today's slate (11.17), making this one of the more watchable matchups on the board, driven almost entirely by pitching.

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Two division rivals, a Wrigley Field showdown between NL Central leaders, and both offenses swinging hot bats make this a legitimately watchable Tuesday matinee-turned-primetime affair. The Cubs and Brewers enter this four-game series as division heavyweights, with the Cubs ending August and beginning September with a key four-game set against the NL Central leaders, and Chicago coming off a statement win, having crushed Milwaukee 17-3 in the series opener on Monday. The Cubs' tNERD (10.81) is elite thanks to a lineup that's been mashing all year and a defense that's been vacuuming up outs, though their bullpen has been a genuine liability all season. Milwaukee counters with plus baserunning and a strong pen, plus a roster that's younger and cheaper than most.

On the mound, Robert Gasser is a fill-in success story — he stepped in to finish out Dustin May's start against the Mets last week, going 5 1/3 innings with one run allowed on six hits and two walks, striking out six to earn the win. His pNERD of 4.88 reflects modest peripherals but a bit of positive regression coming. Matthew Boyd, an All-Star last year, has cooled lately — he's taken the loss in two of his last three starts, allowing 13 runs over 17 1/3 innings against the Cardinals, Mariners, and D-backs — though he's historically dominant at Wrigley. Combined gNERD of 14.78 sits comfortably above today's 11.17 average, making this one of the sharper watches on the slate.

San Francisco Giants @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 3:40p

Summary

Two three-time All-Stars trading pitches at PNC Park is reason enough to tune in, and Paul Skenes' velocity and swing-and-miss stuff make him the best arm on the mound anywhere in baseball today. The Pirates (67-71) have won two straight and are clinging to fringe playoff hopes as they open a season-critical six-game homestand, while the Giants arrive limping defensively but riding some positive batted-ball luck that suggests better days ahead. Skenes, still chasing his first career win over San Francisco, brings a 10.34 pNERD built on elite xFIP-, a mid-90s heater, and youth on his side — comfortably the headliner here, especially with Skenes hasn't recorded a win since July 19 despite the strong underlying numbers. Peralta's pNERD of 4.46 reflects a rocky transition to Tampa Bay, and he's allowed five home runs in 27.1 innings as a Ray, and a homer-prone arm in a dome can produce a crooked number quickly. Manaea, whose 5.73 pNERD is buoyed by a slow pace and some positive regression looming, has quietly owned the Rays over his career—he's 3-1 with a 2.02 ERA in six outings (five starts) against the Rays—though his last few turns have been shaky. The Rays' offense brings thump but not much barrel authority per their tNERD components, while the Mets counter with better bullpen depth. At a 10.11 gNERD, this lands almost exactly at the historical median—watchable mostly for the grudge-match flavor rather than the raw talent on the mound.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Chicago Cubs, 4:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's runaway NL Central lead versus Chicago's fading hope makes this a genuine race-relevant tilt, and it comes with the top gNERD score of the day — well above even the historically hot 95th percentile. The Brewers, division leaders at 85-52, roll into Wrigley for the first of four with the Cubs sitting eight games back after briefly closing to 3.0; Bleacher Nation frames the whole set as a series where the Cubs were roughly five to six games back before briefly cutting it to 3.0 games on August 14, only for that hope to fade fast. Both lineups grade out near the top of the league in tNERD, with Chicago's fielding and batting runs standing out and Milwaukee's baserunning and bullpen doing the heavy lifting, though the Cubs' shaky bullpen (tNERD component of -1.40) is the one real soft spot.

On the mound, Kyle Harrison brings a sparkling xFIP- and a well-below-average pace that makes him one of the more watchable arms around, and he's been nearly untouchable in stretches — striking out 10 Pirates over five innings on August 5, then holding Seattle to two hits across five scoreless frames on August 18 — though he hasn't finished a sixth inning in his last four starts as Milwaukee manages his workload. Clay Holmes, meanwhile, has been arguably better lately: he came over from the Mets at the trade deadline and has been outstanding since joining the rotation on August 8, posting a 1.96 ERA across 23 innings, including seven scoreless on two hits against Arizona last time out. His modest pNERD reflects a lower strikeout rate than you'd expect given those results, but the underlying skill marks (xFIP-, strike rate) are solid enough to make this a legitimately compelling pitching matchup atop a high-stakes divisional series.

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

Miami’s Ryan Gusto has quietly been terrific lately, and Washington counters with a rookie making his first career start — that combination alone makes this worth a look, even if the standings say otherwise. Gusto has pitched 9 2/3 scoreless innings over his past two starts, including 5 2/3 shutout innings in a 4-0 win against the Boston Red Sox, and his pNERD of 4.65 (driven mostly by a strong strike rate) reflects genuine recent quality, not just a hot streak. Across the plate, Will Dion makes his first major-league start after 18 relief appearances, which changes the entire shape of Washington's pitching plan — a true unknown quantity with a pNERD of 0 simply because we have no starter track record to grade yet. The bigger story is the teams: both Miami (9.46 tNERD) and Washington (8.54 tNERD) land comfortably above the historical average, pushing this to a 13.83 gNERD — solidly ahead of the historic 10.81 mean and above today's own 11.07 average, thanks largely to strong baserunning and youth on both sides. Washington's bullpen has been dreadful with a collective 4.60 ERA over the last 10 games, and opposing hitters have hit 12 home runs against Washington's pitchers — expect fireworks if it's still a game by the seventh inning.

Seattle Mariners @ Boston Red Sox, 3:45p

Summary

Both Seattle and Boston are limping toward September, but the pitching matchup makes this one worth a look. Payton Tolle, Boston's 23-year-old rookie lefty, has been the story of the Red Sox summer: Boston counters with rookie left-hander Payton Tolle, who has ascended to nearly the top of the rotation as the season has evolved, and has been especially impressive during August, including eight shutout innings against Toronto and a career-high 14 strikeouts against Oakland. That form shows up in his 9.82 pNERD, built on elite strike-throwing and a nasty whiff rate, plus the youth bonus of doing it all at 23. George Kirby isn't far behind at 7.63 pNERD, thanks to plus velocity and strong command, and he's coming off a bounce-back outing where he allowed just one earned run over 7⅔ innings while striking out nine against Philadelphia. On the team side, Boston's tNERD (6.83) benefits from a strong bullpen and some positive batting luck, while Seattle's 1.76 mark reflects rough fielding and baserunning numbers, and the Mariners are on a four-game losing streak heading into Fenway. The 13.02 gNERD lands comfortably above average both historically and among today's slate, driven almost entirely by the pitching — this is a start-focused watch, not a slugfest.

San Diego enters cratering offensively—San Diego's bats have been cold, hitting just .187 over their past five games with a .271 slugging percentage—having just absorbed a rough weekend at Tampa Bay that fueled the current slide. Michael King, however, has quietly been excellent: averaging just 1.88 earned runs over his last 10 starts while going six or more innings in eight of them, and his pNERD (3.68) undersells how sharp he's been lately, even if his underlying xFIP- and strike rates are middling. Brady Singer is the opposite story—scuffling badly, allowing three-plus earned runs in seven straight starts with five-plus hits in each—though his positive luck component suggests some bad-BABIP regression toward better results might be overdue.

The Padres' tNERD (9.28) is well above the historic 95th percentile threshold, fueled by a strong bullpen and above-average defense, while the Reds check in at a middling 4.73, dragged down by a bottom-of-the-barrel batting-runs figure. Combined gNERD of 10.94 sits almost exactly at the historic median and roughly in line with today's slate average—watchable if it's on, skippable if something shinier is available.

Detail

Cincinnati Reds @ Chicago Cubs, 4:20p

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 1:05p

Summary

Two of the majors' hottest arms right now, and the numbers back it up — this is the best gNERD score of the day and near the top of the season's charts. Cade Cavalli has been the Nationals' unlikely revelation, riding a stretch where he's won four straight decisions and racked up 169 strikeouts, and his 7.66 pNERD (comfortably above today's average) reflects filthy peripherals — a 77 xFIP- and mid-90s heat, even if his deliberate pace docks him a bit. Across the mound, Alcantara, in his second season back from Tommy John surgery, is returning to his Cy Young Award form, and has allowed either one or zero runs in seven of his past 10 starts — he'll also make his 198th career start, passing Ricky Nolasco for the Marlins' all-time record. Both lineups pull their weight too: Washington's offense grades out well above average on batting runs and barrel rate, while Miami counters with elite baserunning and the game's positive underlying-luck signal suggesting more offense than their results show. The Nationals' bullpen is a legitimate soft spot, so if the starters tire, expect the scoring to open up late. Overall, a rare case where the pitching matchup and the underlying team metrics are both pulling in the same direction — appointment viewing for a Saturday.

Team-wise, it's lopsided: Baltimore's 6.04 tNERD (thanks to barrels and bullpen) dwarfs Oakland's 1.89, a roster hurt badly by a middling offense and shaky glovework. At 9.25, the gNERD sits below today's average of 10.35 — watchable for the pitching intrigue, skippable if you need offense.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Two-time reigning AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal returns to Comerica Park for the first time since Detroit shipped him to LA at the deadline, and that alone makes this the day's marquee watch. This is genuinely the day's best game on paper too, with a 15.59 gNERD comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, driven almost entirely by Skubal's 12.30 pNERD — elite strikeout stuff (30% K rate) paired with a minuscule xFIP- of 63. The emotional subplot writes itself: Skubal was dealt from Detroit to Los Angeles after spending his entire career with the Tigers, and now returns to face his former teammates for the first time as a visitor in what should be an emotional night. He's been sharp in LA, too — posting a 3.38 ERA with the Dodgers and striking out 11 over seven innings in his last outing. Detroit counters with journeyman Drew Anderson, a respectable 7.41 pNERD but a converted reliever who is 4-5 with a 4.09 ERA across 44 appearances, moving into the rotation only after the deadline trades of Skubal and Casey Mize. The Dodgers' 8.19 tNERD dwarfs Detroit's 3.27, and with the Dodgers freshly swept by Atlanta and the Tigers having lost 11 of their last 14, both sides have something to play for tonight beyond the reunion narrative.

Miami Marlins @ Washington Nationals, 3:45p

Summary

A hard-throwing 23-year-old ace against a rookie who can't find the plate — this one's got a legitimate watchability edge. Eury Pérez brings a 98-plus mph fastball and elite whiff stuff, and he's been dealing lately: Perez is 2-0 with a 0.50 ERA in his past three starts, with 16 strikeouts and 10 walks over 18 innings. He already torched this same Nationals lineup days ago, having allowed two runs (one earned) on three hits over five innings in a 4-2 victory. His 7.91 pNERD is well above average thanks to velocity, youth, and swing-and-miss ability, though his walk tendencies and a below-average pace knock a bit off the shine. On the other side, rookie Jackson Kent is making just his fourth big-league start, and the results have been rough — Jackson Kent has walked 11 batters in just 12.1 innings, and no stats were reliable enough to generate a pNERD score, so treat him as an unknown wildcard rather than a proven arm. Both offenses actually have some juice — Washington's lineup grades out well on barrels and baserunning despite an ugly bullpen, and Miami's is young, cheap, and running hot — pushing both team NERDs near 9. Combined, the 15.55 gNERD sits comfortably above today's average and near the historic 95th percentile, making this one worth catching, mismatched arms and all.

Boston Red Sox @ New York Yankees, 4:15p

Summary

A Yankee ace with legitimate Cy Young buzz against a fading Red Sox comeback story makes this one worth clearing your evening for. Cam Schlittler has quietly turned into the story of the Yankees' season — a Walpole, Massachusetts native who's this close to a Cy Young case, and his 10.59 pNERD (among the highest scores tracked today, well above the 95th percentile) backs it up: dazzling xFIP-, plate discipline stats, and mid-upper-90s velocity from a 25-year-old who's allowed but one run over six innings against the Blue Jays last time out. Bad news for run support — the Yankees have lost four of his last five starts — but that's irrelevant to how fun he is to watch. Patrick Sandoval, by contrast, is scuffling back from 2024 elbow surgery and his pNERD sits at a middling 2.75, dragged down by a slow pace and shaky command, though he did rebound with two runs over five against the Giants. The larger plot: Boston was 14 games under .500 in June and has since ripped off a 41-14 stretch to get back into wild-card contention, adding real juice to this AL East rivalry game. Both tNERDs sit above average, with the Yankees' bullpen, barrel rate and baserunning all strong. A 14.16 gNERD lands comfortably above both the historical median and today's average — tune in for Schlittler if nothing else.

Summary

Two lousy AL clubs padding stat lines against each other, but a few threads make it mildly watchable if you're bored and it's on.   • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

This one's a near-must-watch, headlined by the best arm in baseball right now. Jacob Misiorowski brings a 15.57 pNERD — comfortably the highest of any pitcher in today's slate — built on a triple-digit fastball and swing-and-miss stuff that's produced a 1.68 ERA this season and two earned runs or fewer in four of his last five outings. He's not just good, he's historically good: the difference last season, though, was that Jacob Misiorowski wasn't quite Jacob Misiorowski yet, but now he's having one of the best seasons in baseball history. Manaea, by contrast, is a league-average arm on the mound (5.60 pNERD) coming off consecutive four-run outings, though his elite pace keeps him watchable in short bursts. The Brewers own the top tNERD score of the day at 9.92, fueled by strong baserunning and bullpen work, and they've dominated this series and rivalry broadly — the Milwaukee Brewers are 18-6 against the New York Mets since April 2023. The Mets counter with a solid broadcast crew and Lindor chasing a homer, but this game's appeal is really about watching a generational fastball humble a fading Mets lineup. At 18.28 gNERD, it's near the top of today's games and well above the historical average.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

A genuine ace-on-ace pitching matchup with playoff stakes attached — this one's worth clearing your schedule for. Chris Sale and Yoshinobu Yamamoto rank second and third in the NL in ERA, respectively, and both come in riding excellent underlying numbers to match, which is exactly the kind of era-defying, throwback pitching duel this sport doesn't offer often enough.

In an August series that has felt more like October baseball, a pair of star pitchers with playoff experience will highlight a game with postseason implications. The Dodgers enter riding a six-game winning streak but now try to avoid their first sweep by the Braves since May 2013, after the Braves won the first two games in dramatic fashion — 4-3 on Tuesday before Ha-Seong Kim delivered a walk-off RBI single Wednesday, his first hit since June 3. Sale's stuff is elite (10.05 pNERD, boosted by a sparkling xFIP-) even if the Braves' offense has left him hanging — he's pitched three straight quality starts in August only to lose each one as Atlanta's bats have produced just five runs across three games. Yamamoto isn't far behind at 7.97 pNERD, and he's 1-0 with 10 scoreless innings in two career outings against Atlanta, including a one-hitter in a 2-1 win last year. With gNERD at 15.94 — comfortably above both the historical 95th percentile (15.60) and today's slate average (11.70) — and the Dodgers' top-tier lineup (8.26 tNERD) lurking behind Yamamoto, this has both craftsmanship and drama.

This one's a bit of a laugher-turned-slugfest series, but the pitching matchup itself won't make anyone rearrange their DVR. Baltimore and St. Louis have spent this series trading haymakers — Pete Alonso and Leody Taveras homered early Wednesday and Christian Encarnacion-Strand went 4-for-5 with a tiebreaking ninth-inning double as Baltimore blew a 7-0 lead before escaping with an 8-7 win. St. Louis is scuffling badly — the Cardinals have lost five straight, and during that skid their starters have allowed 25 runs on 35 hits in 22 innings — which helps explain their thin tNERD despite a young, cheap roster that actually grades out well on age and payroll. Houston hangs on to the top of a mediocre AL West by half a game, while New York fights for pole position in a crowded East race—so there's real stakes here, even if the on-paper numbers are lopsided.
